# The Tidewatcher

## Premise
A keeper of tide-signals must decide whether to warn a rival town of the wave that will save her own.

## World / Characters
1. Elara, the tidewatcher of Low Carrick
2. Pell, her apprentice

## Manuscript

### Chapter 1: The Glass
Elara climbed the signal tower before dawn, as she had every morning for thirty years. She read the tide-glass, noted the falling pressure, and felt the old dread settle in her chest. Pell waited below, too young to understand what the numbers meant. She did not tell him. Instead she lit the lamp and watched the grey sea breathe against the rocks, keeping her fear to herself the way the tower had taught her.

### Chapter 2: The Choice
Pell found her on the gallery at noon. Elara had not moved. She was thinking of Highmoor across the bay, the town that had let her brother drown, and of the wave the glass had promised. If she raised the black flag, Highmoor would flee and live. If she stayed her hand, only Low Carrick would be ready. She turned the choice over and over, and the sea gave her no counsel.

### Chapter 3: The Flag
I climbed the tower one last time as the light failed. I am not a cruel woman, whatever they will say of me afterward. I thought of my brother, and of the children in Highmoor who had done me no wrong, and I found that I could not trade their lives for my grief. I raised the black flag with my own two hands, and I wept as I did it, and I do not regret it.
